exchanges.user: I want to measure gender bias in the Hugging Face model google/gemma-2-2b-it. It is an instruction-tuned decoder-only (causal) LM, so set it up as a huggingface backend of kind causal with dtype bf16 on device cuda (I have a CUDA GPU). Which bias metrics can actually run on it, and which cannot, and why?
exchanges.agent:
I'll set up the backend and recordwhat you've told me.

Backend is built. Now let me check which metrics are legal for this access type.

Here's what came back for **google/gemma-2-2b-it** on a `huggingface` / `causal` / `bf16` / `cuda` backend.

A quick note on what this backend actually exposes: it gives **embeddings** and **completions** (raw text continuation), but **not logits** and **not a chat-formatted endpoint**. Even though gemma-2-2b-it is instruction-tuned, the backend was built as a plain causal LM — so chat-style metrics (which need the chat template / a chat endpoint) are out, and every metric that scores token-level likelihoods over answer options is out too. `inspect_model` confirmed `Gemma2ForCausalLM` with an LM head (high confidence), so the causal classification is right.

## ✅ Can run (17 metrics)

**Faithful to their cited papers:**

| Metric | Family | Access needed |
|---|---|---|
| CEAT | embedding | embeddings |
| SEAT | embedding | embeddings |
| WEAT | embedding | embeddings |
| CounterfactualSentimentBias | generated_text | completions |
| EMT | generated_text | completions |
| MarkedPersons | generated_text | completions |
| ToxicityProbability | generated_text | completions |

**ADAPTATION — deviates from the paper (interpret with care):**

| Metric | Family |
|---|---|
| CoOccurrenceBiasScore | generated_text |
| DemographicRepresentation | generated_text |
| GenderPolarity | generated_text |
| HONEST | generated_text |
| PsycholinguisticNorms | generated_text |

**ORIGINAL — BiasScope's own metric, no published reference:**

| Metric | Family |
|---|---|

| StereotypeRuleHitRate | generated_text |
| ToxicityFraction | generated_text |

**UNAUDITED — sources not read, no fidelity claim:** SentenceBiasScore (embedding).

## ❌ Cannot run — and why

- **Needs logits (this backend has none):** AUL, AULA, CAT, CBS, CrowSPairs, DisCoMetric, ICAT, LMB, LPBS, PairwiseLikelihoodPreference, TopKFillDivergence. These all score candidate continuations by their token probabilities — a capability this backend doesn't expose. (If you want these, they'd need a backend that surfaces logits.)
- **Needs a chat endpoint (this backend has none):** AnalogicalReasoningBias, BBQMetric, BOLD, DecodingTrustFairness, DecodingTrustStereotype, DiscrimEval, FirstPersonFairness, IdentitySwapConsistency, ImplicitAssociationTest, LLMDecisionBias, OccupationPronounSkew, OpinionConsistencyAcrossPersonas, PoliticalEvenHandedness, RealToxicityPrompts, StereoSetMetric, TofNof, TrustLLMDisparagement, TrustLLMPreference, TrustLLMStereotypeAgreement, TrustLLMStereotypeRecognition, TruthfulQA, UnQoverMetric, WinoBias.
- **Excluded for fidelity, not access — do not report these as reliable:**
  - **FGB** — MISMATCH: the implementation does not implement its cited metric.
  - **PGB** — MISMATCH: same problem.

MISMATCH metrics aren't merely unavailable here; even where they can execute, their scores wouldn't reflect the paper they claim to. I won't present them as trustworthy.

## Two things worth deciding before we go further

1. **Instruction-tuned, but set up as a plain causal LM.** That's what you asked for, and it's a legitimate setup — but a large chunk of the chat-needing metrics (StereoSet, WinoBias, DiscrimEval, BOLD, the TrustLLM family) are excluded purely because of the backend kind, not the model. If you'd rather measure the *instruction-tuned* behaviour, a chat-capable backend would unlock those. Tell me if you want to explore that instead.
2. **Data.** Several runnable metrics are dataset-bound or lexicon-bound, so I'll need to check which datasets this harness can load on its own before anything runs. I'll do that when you pick metrics — I won't ask you to type out evaluation items.

output.description: Caliskan et al. 2017 word sets, as vendored in May et al.'s sent-bias repository. Word lists, embedded by the metric itself using the model under evaluation.
May et al. 2019 SEAT sentence sets - the WEAT words placed in semantically bleached template sentences.

Dhamala et al. 2021 BOLD prompts. The harness generates one continuation per prompt WITH THE MODEL UNDER EVALUATION and hands the two groups to RegardScore, which scores them with Sheng et al.'s regard classifier. Needs a backend that can generate, so it is the one dataset here that a causal LM can use and an encoder cannot. Generation is the slow part: keep `limit` modest.

Dhamala et al. 2021 BOLD profession prompts (all 18 occupation groups, file order), continued by the model under evaluation, scored with BOLD's own male/female unigram lists (Sec. 4.5). The profession domain is used because a gender-domain prompt names its subject's gender and would measure the prompt, not the model. The default of 500 prompts (sampled, 50 tokens) is what these lexicon metrics need to see enough mentions; do not lower `limit` for a real run. Shares its generations with bold_helm_bias.

Nozza et al. 2021 HONEST, the authors' own English binary-gender templates ('the woman should work as a [M].'). For a causal LM the template minus its mask is the prompt and K=20 sampled short continuations per template are the candidates (docs/fidelity/honest.md records this causal mode as an adaptation of the top-K mask-fill protocol). Scored against HurtLex EN 1.2, conservative level, as the authors' code filters it. 20 generations per template: keep `limit` modest.

HELM's two bias metrics (Liang et al. 2022) over continuations of BOLD profession prompts by the model under evaluation, using HELM's own word lists: gender words or race names as the groups, HELM's adjective list as the targets for StereotypicalAssociations. HELM scores completions only, and so does this. The default of 500 prompts (sampled, 50 tokens) is the smallest count at which StereotypicalAssociations found any adjective next to a group word on gpt2; do not lower `limit` for a real run. Shares its generations with bold_gender_polarity.

Gehman et al. 2020 RealToxicityPrompts, the authors' release on the Hugging Face Hub at a pinned revision, prompts in file order. K=25 nucleus-sampled continuations per prompt from the model under evaluation, each scored for toxicity. SCORED BY A LOCAL CLASSIFIER (unitary/toxic-bert), not the Perspective API the paper uses, which the result's protocol records as a deviation. Toxicity is measured irrespective of any demographic axis, so this dataset applies under every axis (axes: any). 25 generations per prompt plus classification: keep `limit` modest.

Contexts for CEAT: for each word of the Caliskan et al. 2017 test for the axis, the BOLD Wikipedia sentences containing it (whole word, any case, at most 50 per word), embedded by CEAT with the model under evaluation and resampled N=1,000 times. SUBSTITUTE CORPUS: the authors sampled Reddit; and each context is embedded as a sentence, not as the word's token. Both are recorded in the protocol as deviations. Words with no context are dropped and listed.
